claims.text: The starting material is a homogeneous high-entropy alloy without an intentional low-shear-strength phase or segregated surface layer.
The proposed intervention is addition of approximately 1–2 at.% Ag to the HEA during synthesis.
Adding approximately 1–2 at.% Ag will cause Ag to segregate to the contact surface during service.
Ag segregation will form a continuous Ag-rich surface film.
Alternatively, the surface-localized Ag-rich structure may consist of nanoclusters.
Elevated temperature and frictional loading will drive Ag atoms in the doped HEA toward the surface.
Surface-segregated Ag atoms will coalesce into a lubricious film.
The Ag-rich layer will have sufficiently low shear strength to act as a solid lubricant.
The Ag-rich layer will minimize direct metal-to-metal contact.
Minimizing direct metal-to-metal contact will reduce friction and limit wear.
The Ag addition will reduce both coefficient of friction and wear rate relative to the undoped HEA.
The coefficient of friction may decrease by approximately 30–50% relative to the undoped HEA.
The wear rate may decrease by approximately a factor of 2–3 relative to the undoped HEA.
The beneficial tribological effect is expected under sliding or reciprocating wear from room temperature to approximately 500–600 °C.
The effect will persist only in atmospheres where oxidation does not remove the Ag-rich film.
Effective lubrication requires a temperature high enough to mobilize Ag for surface segregation.
Temperatures causing rapid oxidation or Ag-film depletion will eliminate or weaken the benefit.
Extremely aggressive oxidative or mechanical conditions may overcome stabilization by the Ag-rich layer.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis specifies a continuous Ag-rich film, whereas the structural mediator allows either a layer or nanoclusters; isolated nanoclusters do not necessarily constitute the claimed continuous film.

Effectiveness is predicted from room temperature, but the stated mechanism emphasizes elevated-temperature diffusion and the boundary requires a temperature sufficient to mobilize Ag; no threshold or alternative room-temperature segregation mechanism is supplied.
